test_method.procedure_description: Pyrex cell with ground-glass joints in a temperature-controlled air thermostat; total immersion usually used to reach steady conditions. First potentiostatically polarized at the least noble passive-region potential for at least 15 min; potential advanced in 50 mV stages with 5 min between changes. Subsequently held at fixed potentials for long periods and examined under a low-power microscope; the lowest potential showing pitting after at least 10 h defined steady-state Vc.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Steadily increasing current indicated non-steady-state onset; pitting confirmed microscopically. Steady-state Vc required pitting after 10 h or longer at fixed potential.

experiments.result_note: Table footnote: estimated from data for various chloride concentrations. Material: Ni. Potentials discussed on the hydrogen scale; the raw anchored unit is retained. The general reported reproducibility is about ±5 mV, without adding uncertainty to the locked reading.

alloy.preparation: Vacuum melted from pure components in dense alumina; melt drawn into 7 mm Vycor tubes under Ar or He and water quenched; homogenized in Ar or He, usually 1050–1100 °C for several hours. Cold rolled to 0.25 cm, annealed at 1000–1050 °C and water quenched; lower-Cr alloy ingots also described as swaged to approximately 0.45 cm rods, annealed at 1050 °C and water quenched. Electrodes abraded to final 3/0 emery paper and usually pickled in 15% HNO3 + 5% HF at 80 °C for 5 min to remove the cold-worked surface.

Subsequently held at fixed potentials for long periods and examined under a low-power microscope; the lowest potential showing pitting after at least 10 h defined steady-state Vc.
test_method.pitting_criterion: Steadily increasing current indicated non-steady-state onset; pitting confirmed microscopically. Steady-state Vc required pitting after 10 h or longer at fixed potential.

experiments.result_note: Approximate graphical reading. Material: 15% Cr, 13% Ni. Potentials discussed on the hydrogen scale; the raw anchored unit is retained. The general reported reproducibility is about ±5 mV, without adding uncertainty to the locked reading.

alloy.preparation: Vacuum melted from pure components in dense alumina; melt drawn into 7 mm Vycor tubes under Ar or He and water quenched; homogenized in Ar or He, usually 1050–1100 °C for several hours. Stainless-steel ingots swaged to approximately 0.45 cm rods, annealed at 1050 °C and water quenched. Electrodes abraded to final 3/0 emery paper and usually pickled in 15% HNO3 + 5% HF at 80 °C for 5 min to remove the cold-worked surface.
alloy.microstructure: Single-phase structure confirmed metallographically for the relatively low-Cr, high-Ni stainless-steel series.

test_solution.preparation: Deaerated with purified nitrogen (gas passed over Cu at 450 °C); nitrogen did not flow during actual measurements.
